definition_used: Delta_phi = accumulated unwrapped rotation angle of n_v(t) = v1(t) x v2(t) (normalized), the normal to the plane spanned by the two quirks' lab-frame velocity vectors, relative to n_v at the first valid sample. This is the Eq.8/9 and Fig.3-axis-label quantity ('Delta_phi'), not the caption's unsupported 'Delta_theta' (no equation anywhere defines a separate Delta_theta; treated as a paper-internal caption/axis-label inconsistency, confirmed by direct visual inspection of the rendered PDF in a prior turn).
reference_plane: plane spanned by v1(t), v2(t) at each instant (paper's own words, Eq.8 preamble)
sign_convention: unsigned (angle via arccos of dot product; normal-vector sign ambiguity resolved by flipping to the same hemisphere as the reference sample, since a plane's normal has no intrinsic orientation)
radial_coordinate: r = |x_cm(t)| = |(x1(t)+x2(t))/2|, in cm (GeV^-1 -> cm via hbar*c)
paper_reference_scale: Eq.9 order-of-magnitude ~1e-5 (v_cm/v^2)(B/2T)(2keV/Lambda)^2; text states typical values 'somewhat larger than 1e-5 ... not larger than 1e-3'; Fig.3's own y-axis spans 0.0-0.4 (x1e-3), i.e. up to ~4e-4 rad.
b_field_role: Lorentz force on each quirk (charge +-2/3 e) from uniform B=2T along lab z-axis; identical B-field treatment used everywhere else in this project (quirk_trajectory.py, unmodified).
isr_recoil_role: NOT modeled in this diagnostic (no ISR jet 4-momentum injected) -- this is a PROJECT SIMPLIFICATION consistent with all other trajectory work in this project to date (ISR only affects overall CM boost magnitude/direction, which this scan explores directly and parametrically via beta_cm_vec instead).
what_is_measured: the plane spanned by the two quirks' instantaneous LAB-FRAME VELOCITY VECTORS (v1 x v2 direction) -- NOT a fit to detector hits, NOT the fitted-plane normal n3 from coplanarity_fit.py's Sec IIIC algorithm (that is a DIFFERENT quantity: a best-fit plane to discrete hit positions, used for Fig.4/5, not Fig.3). Fig.3 is about the TRUE underlying kinematic plane rotation, prior to and independent of any detector reconstruction.
key_finding: CORRECTED CONCLUSION (supersedes both this session's earlier attempt and the prior turn's 'NOT ACHIEVED' verdict): the originally-reported 'geometric degeneracy' (Delta_phi == 0 exactly for configs A-D, an angular-momentum-vector-based proxy used in the prior turn) was a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, not real physics, traced to two compounding bugs: (1) using L = x_rel x p_rel as the measured plane instead of the paper's own stated definition (Eq.8 preamble: 'the plane spanned by the quirks' velocity vectors', i.e. n_v = v1 x v2); (2) even after switching to n_v, an initial validity threshold (|n_v| > 1e-9*max) was too loose and let through samples near the periodic near-antiparallel crossings (v1~-v2, where |v1 x v2|->0 and its direction is numerically ill-conditioned), producing isolated spurious single-sample spikes of order 0.02-0.1 rad that dominated a naive max() statistic and also, in the fully degenerate x-z-confined configs, apparently suppressed all signal to exactly zero under the OLDER angular-momentum proxy. After fixing BOTH issues (correct n_v=v1xv2 definition; percentile-based exclusion of near-crossing samples, valid = |n_v| > 0.1*median(|n_v|)), the SAME simple, unperturbed, natural configuration already used (and validated) for the achieved Figure 2 reproduction (pure-x CM boost beta_cm=0.6, B=2T along z, internal tilt along z -- configs J_colored_natural_config and K_ew_natural_config) reproduces Delta_phi(r) with the CORRECT magnitude (max ~4.6e-4 rad colored, ~6.1e-4 rad EW -- both within the paper's own stated range: Eq.9 order 1e-5, text 'typically ... not larger than 1e-3', Fig.3's own y-axis spanning 0.0-0.4e-3) and the CORRECT qualitative shape (rises smoothly from 0 at r=0, oscillates, accumulates towards a stable plateau by r~15-20cm -- matching the paper's own description verbatim: 'Delta_phi oscillates and slowly accumulates ... until it stabilizes around a fixed value'). No boost perturbation, tilt manipulation, or any other departure from the natural Figure-2 configuration was needed once the observable itself was computed correctly -- this was a bug in HOW Delta_phi was measured, not a missing physical ingredient.
caveat_initial_orientation_unknown: The primary result (configs J, K) uses the same simple, unperturbed initial orientation already used for the achieved Figure 2 reproduction (pure-x CM boost, internal tilt along the B-field axis) -- this specific orientation (relative angle between boost direction and internal-motion tilt) is a PROJECT ASSUMPTION, since the paper does not publish the exact initial conditions of its own representative Fig.2/3 events. A fully first-principles reproduction would instead read the REAL (px1,py1,pz1,px2,py2,pz2) 4-momenta directly from a specific existing signal event (e.g. event 386, already used for Figure 4) -- this is the recommended next experiment below.
caveat_residual_spike_artifacts: The final plot still shows occasional sharp spikes/dips at a handful of isolated r values (visible in Figure_3_diagnostic_v2.png, e.g. colored curve near r~5,15cm). These occur where the percentile-based validity filter transitions between 'valid' segments separated by a near-degenerate gap; the reference direction is re-anchored to the first sample of each new segment, which can introduce a small discontinuity at the segment boundary. The underlying smooth trend BETWEEN spikes (the majority of each curve) is the real, validated signal (confirmed by the percentile statistics: median ~6e-5, p95~1.4e-4, p99~4e-4 rad, all physically reasonable and NOT dominated by the spikes). This is a known, documented limitation of this diagnostic's post-hoc angle-unwrapping method, not a claim that the plotted curve is spike-free like the paper's own (smoother) Fig.3 -- reported honestly, not smoothed away.
recommended_next_experiment: (1) Take one specific existing signal event from the authoritative colored-quirk CSV (e.g. event 386, already used for Figure 4), extract its REAL (px1,py1,pz1,px2,py2,pz2) 4-momenta, and recompute Delta_phi(r) directly from quirk_trajectory.py's own trajectory output for that exact event -- a fully first-principles single-event reproduction. (2) Replace the post-hoc arccos/hemisphere-flip angle-unwrapping with a running-integral of the instantaneous angular velocity of n_v(t) (d(n_v_hat)/dt cross n_v_hat), which would not require a discrete reference sample at all and should eliminate the residual segment-boundary spikes noted above.
no_manual_curve_shaping: No curve was reshaped, smoothed, or rescaled after computation. The y-axis unit (x1e-3) and x-axis unit (cm) match the paper's Fig.3 exactly. No parameter was tuned to make the curve resemble the paper's beyond satisfying the explicit acceptance criteria (order-of-magnitude match, nontrivial r-dependence, energy-momentum conservation).
reproducibility: Deterministic ODE integration (no RNG used anywhere in this script) -- identical inputs always give bit-identical outputs.
